title: Bezos-Backed Consortium Led by Indian-Origin Amit Bhatia Acquires 38% Stake in Liverpool FC
excerpt: Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, Lakshmi Mittal's son-in-law Amit Bhatia, and Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin form 1892 Holdings to buy into the Premier League club in a deal valuing it at over $7 billion.
body:
• A consortium called 1892 Holdings, led by British-Indian entrepreneur Amit Bhatia, has acquired a 38% stake in Liverpool FC from Fenway Sports Group
  • The deal values Liverpool at over $7 billion and includes an option for the consortium to become majority shareholders within 12 months at an $8 billion valuation
  • Bhatia, the son-in-law of Indian steel billionaire Lakshmi Mittal, will become Liverpool's vice chairman and join the club's expanded board

Jeff Bezos has made his first foray into sports ownership, and the deal comes wrapped in deep Indian business connections. A consortium called 1892 Holdings, led by British-Indian entrepreneur Amit Bhatia and backed by Amazon founder Bezos and Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin, has acquired a 38% stake in Liverpool Football Club from majority owners Fenway Sports Group.

The deal, confirmed by FSG on August 14, values Liverpool at more than $7 billion (£5.2 billion), making it one of the richest transactions in global sports history. FSG, which purchased the Premier League club for £300 million in 2010, retains majority ownership and operational control.

The Indian Connection

Bhatia, 46, is the central figure in the consortium. Married to Vanisha Mittal Bhatia, daughter of Indian steel billionaire Lakshmi Mittal, he brings nearly two decades of sports ownership experience. He spent 18 years as a director and co-owner of Queens Park Rangers in London, including five years as chairman, before relinquishing his stake earlier this month.

The Mittal Family Trusts are also part of 1892 Holdings. Earlier this year, Bhatia's father-in-law Lakshmi Mittal acquired a 75% stake in the Rajasthan Royals, one of the most coveted franchises in the Indian Premier League.

Bhatia will become Liverpool's vice chairman and join the club's expanded board alongside Elaine Saverin of EE Capital (wife of Eduardo Saverin) and Bryan Baum of K5 Sports, who represents Bezos. Bezos himself, the world's third-richest person with an estimated net worth of $281 billion, will not hold a board seat.

"To be welcomed as a partner in a club of this stature is a huge privilege. We are making this investment because we believe deeply in Liverpool and its leadership."

— Amit Bhatia, Vice Chairman, Liverpool FC

A Path to Majority Ownership

Sky Sports News reported that the consortium has an option to become majority shareholders of Liverpool within 12 months, at a valuation of approximately $8 billion. Sources stressed that the existence of the agreement does not guarantee a future transaction, but the framework is in place for a potential full takeover.

According to The Wall Street Journal, Bezos was expected to write the largest check among the consortium participants, though his exact investment amount has not been disclosed. He is participating through K5 Global, an investment firm managed by Michael Kives and Bryan Baum.

Liverpool's Rising Valuation

The deal underscores the surging valuations of top-tier football clubs. FSG's $7 billion valuation for Liverpool represents a more than 17-fold return on their 2010 investment. Liverpool are currently the fourth most valuable club in the world, according to Sky Sports.

Under FSG's ownership, Liverpool have won every major trophy available, including the Premier League in 2024-25. The club finished fifth last season and has appointed Andoni Iraola as manager ahead of their new campaign, which opens at Newcastle United on August 23.

Growing Indian Influence in Global Football

The involvement of the Mittal-Bhatia family in Liverpool adds to a growing pattern of Indian business dynasties investing in global sports. Beyond the Rajasthan Royals, the Mittals now have a significant foothold in English football through Liverpool. Bhatia also invests in TGL — the tech-forward golf league created by Rory McIlroy and Tiger Woods — and in Switch Hitter, a cricket media brand founded by Kevin Pietersen.

The deal is subject to regulatory approval from the new Independent Football Regulator and Premier League owners' and directors' tests, a process that could take up to 90 days. Liverpool's supporters' group Spirit of Shankly has already contacted the regulator and is seeking engagement with Bhatia and the consortium.
